The rain arrives not as a visitor but as a returning exile, hammering its fists against the windowpanes with a fury born of long absence. Each droplet carries the weight of forgotten oceans... the memory of clouds that wandered too far from shore.

We speak of weather as though it were small. Inconsequential. A thing to mention between silences. But the storm knows otherwise. It reshapes the gutters into rivers, transforms the ordinary street into a mirror of the bruised sky above.

There is something unravelable about a grey afternoon. The light refuses to commit, hovering between pallor and shadow, casting the world in a hue that has no proper name. The trees bend like penitents. The birds have vanished into whatever secret architecture shelters them from the deluge.

And then, without ceremony... it stops. The silence after rain is not true silence but a held breath, the earth drinking deeply, the roots whispering their ancient gratitude beneath the sodden ground.
